title: Union Pacific conductor who recovered from stroke still posed ‘direct threat’ to safety, court rules
summary: Under the ADA, the railway made an “objectively reasonable” decision to restrict the conductor from driving a train, the 8th Circuit held.

title: DHS to propose end of 60-day grace period for H-1B visa holders
summary: Few details are known without the rule’s text, which has yet to be published in the Federal Register, but the change may pose difficulties for employers, one attorney said.

title: Labor market exhibits ‘continued resilience,’ The Conference Board finds
summary: Multiple factors have made an already complex job market even more volatile this year, per a report.

title: ‘Alienating and cruel’: EEOC files lawsuit against employer for segregating DEI training by race
summary: This iteration of the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission has been vocal about cracking down on DEI in the context of Title VII.

title: This week in 5 numbers: Employees say bosses don’t work as hard
summary: Here’s a roundup of numbers from the last week — including how much Apple will pay to settle U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commissions allegations.

title: Columbia faces discrimination lawsuit from Palestinian employees and students
summary: Plaintiffs allege the Ivy League institution “actively participated in and amplified” racial and political targeting of its campus members.

title: Brookings researchers slam assumptions in work requirements rule
summary: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services are being accused of fudging the data at the center of a rule that makes it harder for Medicaid enrollees to prove they’re exempt from work requirements.

title: Most employers say rising healthcare costs force salary tradeoffs
summary: Employers cited high drug prices, high-cost claims and hospital prices as their biggest threats to affordability.

title: Empathetic leaders drive whether AI is seen as an opportunity or a risk, survey finds
summary: Empathy lifted every AI metric measured, including employee optimism and sense of control over their work, according to a Businessolver report.

title: Mile Hi Foods settles for $1.5M over alleged refusal to hire women, Black and Afghan workers
summary: The complaint alleged that when the HR manager opposed these practices, Mile Hi unlawfully retaliated by harassing and ultimately discharging her.
